answer: Each lantern registers on the prism, a ledger that hashes every work output it submits, so clones copying outputs collide and are rejected. Weight equals the square of attested epochs, and an epoch counts only when the lantern burns ferrous, a non-transferable credit earned solely by its own judged work. A 100-epoch veteran weighs 10,000, so matching it takes 10,000 fresh clones, each doing a real epoch of distinct graded work. It breaks if graders can be fooled by cheap generated output.
